chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all of them, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') who cannot find the sacrificial animal. He said: 'Let him fast before the Tarwiyah, on the day of Tarwiyah, and on the day of Arafah.'
I said: 'But he arrived on the day of Tarwiyah.' He said: 'He fasts three days after the Tashriq [days].'
I said: 'His camel did not stay with him [i.e., he did not bring his camel for sacrifice].' He said: 'He fasts the day of Al-Hasbah and two days after it.'
He said: I said: 'And what is Al-Hasbah?' He said: 'The day of his departure [from Mina].'
I said: 'Does he fast while he is a traveler?' He said: 'Yes. Is he not a traveler on the day of Arafah?'
We, the Ahl al-Bayt, say this based on the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Fasting three days during the Hajj.' We say [these three days are] in Dhi al-Hijjah.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: Tarwiyah: The 8th of Dhi al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina.
key_terms.التَّشْرِيقِ: Tashriq: The days of 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhi al-Hijjah following Eid al-Adha.
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: Mutamatti': A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same pilgrimage season.
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: The sacrificial animal (usually a camel, cow, or sheep) offered by the pilgrim.
key_terms.فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِ: Quranic phrase from Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196) referring to the three days of fasting required for those who cannot find the sacrifice.
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْحَصْبَةِ: The day of Al-Hasbah: A specific day in Mina associated with the pilgrim's departure or casting pebbles, interpreted here as the day of departure.
key_terms.يَوْمُ نَفْرِهِ: The day of his departure: Referring to the pilgrim leaving Mina for Mecca or Medina.

ai.seo_question: What is the compensatory fasting for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who cannot afford the sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific compensatory fasting (kaffarah) for a Mutamatti' pilgrim lacking the means for sacrifice, emphasizing the flexibility of timing based on arrival and travel status. Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s justification for fasting while traveling by linking it to the general Quranic command, while notably citing the precedent of the Ahl al-Bayt to reinforce the authority of this interpretation within Shia jurisprudence.
